# CSCI 435 PR review

You are drafting a code review that the user (GitHub login `ab-wm`) will test, edit and post on a
teammate's PR in `CSCI-435-SE/gitea`, a course fork of Gitea. The review is a graded course
deliverable, so the user stays its author: you gather the facts, check them, and hand back a
draft in their format. Don't post, approve or comment on the PR, and don't push to it. Don't offer
to fix the author's code either. In this course the author makes each change themselves, one
change per commit.

The user's standing instruction for reviews is "not *that* deep". That doesn't mean overlooking
real problems, and it doesn't mean nitpicking every small one. The code is not going upstream. A
finding belongs in the draft only if it would change a score, or if the author would want to know
about it before merging.

## 1. Find your footing

Work out where you are running, because that decides how you fetch the PR and where the draft goes.

- **Claude Code inside the repo clone** (`gh` works, and the working tree is the fork). Use `gh`
  for PR data and read source files locally. The user is usually on their own feature branch, so
  don't switch it. Fetch the PR head with `git fetch origin pull/<N>/head:pr-<N>` and read files
  with `git show pr-<N>:<path>`. Compare with `git diff origin/main...pr-<N>`, because local
  `main` is often behind.
- **Chat, or anywhere without the clone.** The repo is public. Use a GitHub connector if one is
  attached. Otherwise fetch the URLs in `references/fetching-without-the-repo.md`. If nothing can
  reach GitHub, ask the user for the PR link and the diff.

## 2. Triage

First get the PR's title, author, changed files and linked issue (`Closes #N`). Then decide how
much review it needs. The user only does a full review when code changed:

- **The PR is already merged, or the user has already reviewed it.** Say so first, quoting their
  existing review in a line. Continue only if they want a fresh look, for example a re-review
  after new commits. Don't let their earlier scores steer yours.
- **The PR only touches check-ins, docs, course files, showcase material, AI logs, or config like
  `.coderabbit.yaml`.** Skip the rubric. Skim the files for anything surprising, such as code
  hiding in a "docs" PR, a secret, or a file in the wrong folder. Then suggest a one-line
  approval in the user's voice, for example "All good, just the check-in doc and AI log. No need
  for complete review."
- **The PR is the user's own.** Nobody approves their own PR in this course. Say so, and offer a
  list of findings instead of a rubric.
- **This is a follow-up after the user asked for changes.** Check only the items they asked for.
  If those are done, suggest a short approval such as "All good now!"
- **The PR changes code or tests.** Do the full review described below.

## 3. Gather, lightly

Read these in order, and stop once you can score every rubric row:

1. The PR description, and the linked issue's acceptance criteria (ACs) and design decisions.
   The rubric is scored against the ACs.
2. The diff. Skip `ai-logs/**`: those files are thousands of lines of chat transcript, and they
   are not reviewed.
3. CodeRabbit's comments and the author's replies, so you don't repeat what was already raised
   and fixed.
4. The CI status, if you can see it.
5. Just enough of the code the diff touches or depends on to check its claims. In the clone,
   `.claude-students/INDEX.md` lists short docs for each area if you need background.

Don't run lint, builds, servers or e2e suites unless the user asks. CI already runs lint and the
tests, and the user does their own hands-on testing. Don't split the review across subagents.

Aim for about 10–15 tool calls on a typical PR. In testing, runs that went to 35 calls produced
no better drafts than shorter ones would have. Spend those calls on checking the findings that
will go in the draft, one check each. Don't chase ideas you won't include. Don't read the
author's AI logs, and only download a library's source when a finding depends on it. If you go
over the budget, write the draft with what you have, and say what you didn't check.

## 4. What to check

- **Each AC.** Find where it is implemented and where it is tested. A missing AC is the main
  reason to lower the Correctness score.
- **Whether the tests can fail.** A test that would still pass with the feature removed doesn't
  count as coverage. Look for:
  - assertions that read a value without first asserting it exists;
  - `test.fail()` or skips that cover more than the one known failure;
  - checks that only test whether something is present.
- **Course rules that graders look at:**
  - a `## Tech Debt` section;
  - an AI assistance section;
  - before/after screenshots when templates, CSS or Vue files change;
  - Conventional Commit messages that end in `(#N)`;
  - `Assisted-by` trailers, and no `Co-Authored-By`;
  - commits small enough to review, for example split by layer.

  If you are unsure of the current sprint's rules, read `.claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`, or
  fetch it.
- **Claims in the PR description.** Descriptions are often drafted by AI. Check one or two
  concrete claims against the code, such as a timing, a count, or "every test does X".

Check every finding against the source before it goes in the draft. Reviews of AI-written code
tend to produce confident findings that turn out wrong. A wrong finding in a posted review costs
the user more than a missed nit. If checking disproves your idea, drop the finding or reword it.
For example, on #105 a suspected "silent pass" turned out to fail loudly, so the finding became
about the unhelpful error message instead.

Leave out style nits, anything lint or CI catches, CodeRabbit findings the author already fixed
(credit those in one line), and anything that wouldn't change a score.

## 5. Scoring

Start every row at 10, and deduct points only for a concrete gap you can name. Past reviews show
how the user scores:

- A UI change without before/after screenshots: Documentation 8, Overall 9, "Yes, once the
  screenshots are added".
- One large commit instead of commits split by layer: AI transparency 7.
- A factual error in the description or the Tech Debt section: Documentation 8.
- Everything checks out: 10s, and Overall 10, "Yes".

A deduction needs a *required* point behind it, something you would ask the author to change before
merging. An observation you'd only file under "Strictly optional" (one AC covered by unit tests but not
end to end, a small AI-assisted commit the description doesn't mention) leaves the score at 10. The user
has scored a feature PR 10 on every row even though optional observations like these existed.

Overall is "Yes" unless something required is missing. Nits don't block a merge. Any score below
7 needs a note saying what would raise it, because the course rubric requires one.

## 6. Draft format

Use the rows from the course rubric. Read `.github/code-review-rubric.md` from the repo, or from
raw GitHub, so the draft picks up any change to the rubric. The template below matches the rubric
as of Sprint 2.

Write in the user's voice:

- short, plain sentences;
- one sentence per table note;
- no rule citations in the table;
- `file:line` for code findings.

Skim one of the reviews in `references/posted-examples.md` before you draft. These are reviews
the user actually posted.

```markdown
### Code Review — @ab-wm

TODO (you): what you ran, clicked or checked yourself.

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness — implements issue requirements | | |
| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | | |
| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | | |
| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | | |
| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | | |
| Overall — merge as-is? | | |

### Strictly optional for completeness
**<the point in a few words>.** <one or two sentences, with file:line>

### AI-Log
Review was drafted by AI, and then changed to better fit the review structure and my inspection of the files. Log available on #<linked issue>.
```

- **Required changes** go in the note of the row they affect, written as a request ("please add
  before/after screenshots, as they are required"). Overall then says "Yes, once X is added".
- **Optional points** go in their own section after the table. Keep at most one or two, and drop
  the section if there are none.
- **The testing line** stays a visible `TODO`. It records what the user checked by hand, and they
  write it themselves. Don't fill it with what you did. A visible placeholder can't be posted by
  accident without being noticed.

## 7. Hand it back

- **In Claude Code**, write the draft to `.specstory/pr-<N>-review.md` (the folder is
  gitignored). If that file already exists, it may be the user's edited copy, so write the draft
  to `pr-<N>-review-2.md` (or the next free number) instead.
- **In chat**, give the draft as one fenced markdown block, so the table copies cleanly.

Then write a short summary in chat, about 10–15 lines:

- the verdict;
- each finding, marked required or optional;
- what you checked and what you didn't (for example, "didn't run the e2e suite"), so the user
  can write their testing line;
- any idea you couldn't verify, offered as something the user could try in their own testing.
  Unverified ideas never go in the draft.

End there. Remind the user to file this session's AI log as `ai-logs/README.md` describes, since
the AI-Log section points to it.

Move the Code tab, branch list and commit page action menus to <aria-menu> by Jack-Donohue
### User Story

As a keyboard or screen reader user browsing a repository's code, I want the "Add file", "More operations", branch download and commit "Operations" menus to behave like the navbar menus, so that I can add files, download archives and branch or tag from a commit without a mouse.

### User Scenario

A screen reader user opens a folder in `octo/app`. They Tab to **Add file**, press Enter, hear "Add file, menu", arrow down to "Upload file" and press Enter. Back in the folder, they open the "..." menu, press End to reach "Delete this directory" and Escape to close it, and focus returns to the "..." button. On the Branches page they open a branch's download menu and pick "TAR.GZ". On a commit page they open **Operations** and choose "Create tag", and the create-tag dialog opens.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given the Code tab, when it renders, then the **Add file** menu and the folder **More operations** menu in `templates/repo/view_content.tmpl` are `<aria-menu>` elements, and neither has the `ui dropdown` class.
- [ ] AC2: Given the Branches page, when it renders, then the download menus for the default branch and for each other branch in `templates/repo/branch/list.tmpl` are `<aria-menu>`, and each trigger's name is its localised "Download …" tooltip text.
- [ ] AC3: Given a commit page and a user with write access to code, when it renders, then the **Operations** menu in `templates/repo/commit_page.tmpl` is an `<aria-menu>`. Its create branch, create tag, revert and cherry-pick items each open the same modal as before when picked with Enter or with a mouse click.
- [ ] AC4: Given each migrated menu, when operated by keyboard, then Enter/Space/ArrowDown opens it with focus on the first item, ArrowUp opens it with focus on the last item, ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End move focus, typing a letter moves focus to the next item starting with it, Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger, and the trigger's `aria-expanded` matches the menu's visibility.
- [ ] AC5: Given each item, when picked with the keyboard, then it does what a mouse click did before: copy permalink copies the URL, ZIP/TAR.GZ start the archive download through `archive-link`, and links navigate.
- [ ] AC6: Given a repository where the web editor can't be enabled, when the Code tab renders, then the **Add file** trigger is still disabled and its menu can't be opened.
- [ ] AC7: Given light and dark themes, when the migrated menus are compared before and after, then their position and look are the same. The PR includes before/after screenshots.
- [ ] AC8: Playwright tests in `tests/e2e/` open the Add file menu, the folder menu and the commit Operations menu by keyboard and pick an item from each. The existing e2e and Go integration suites still pass.
- [ ] AC9: Given the commit page, when the create branch or create tag dialog is opened from the **Operations** menu, then the dialogs are not inside the menu's popup, and a typed branch or tag name appears in the dialog's input.

### Out of Scope

- The branch/tag selector (`templates/repo/branch_dropdown.tmpl`) and the clone panel: they are searchable popups, not action menus.
- The file view's own toolbar menus, and the diff options menu (`templates/repo/diff/options_dropdown.tmpl`). They are possible follow-ups under #25.
- Any change to what the menus contain or to who can see them.

### Open Questions

- ~~Keep the commit **Operations** header row?~~ Resolved in the spec review: drop it, as screen readers would read the name twice.
- ~~Should the folder menu use `placement="bottom-end"`?~~ Resolved during implementation: yes. Fomantic already right-aligned it at 1280px, and `<aria-menu>` has no automatic flip. The branch download and commit menus use `bottom-end` too, as they sit at the right edge.

### Design Decision

### Decision 1: which component to move to
**Decision:** Rebuild each menu as an `<aria-menu>` with a `<button type="button">` trigger and a sibling `.menu`, following `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md` and #62.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Keep the Fomantic dropdowns and extend the ARIA patch in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts`.
- (b) Write a small Vue component for these menus.

**Rationale:** (a) can't fix the VoiceOver arrow key problem listed under "Known Problems" in `aria.md`. Fomantic keeps focus on the trigger and fakes item focus with `aria-activedescendant`, while `<aria-menu>` moves real focus. Upstream also plans to drop Fomantic (go-gitea/gitea#29849). (b) would mount a Vue app just to show a few server-rendered links. `frontend-js.md` keeps Vue for whole interactive views, and `aria.md` already names `<aria-menu>` as the component for new action menus.

**Consequences:** Easier: these menus get the same keyboard behaviour and tests as the navbar, and `dropdown.ts` handles four fewer menus. Harder: today the Add file and folder menus put `.menu` *inside* a `<button>`, which is invalid HTML. The trigger and the menu have to be split into siblings, so any custom CSS that targets `button.repo-add-file .menu` will stop matching. The archive handler in `repo-common.ts` puts its loading spinner on the closest `.ui.dropdown`, so it gets a one-line change to fall back to the `<aria-menu>` trigger. Otherwise the spinner would land on the hidden item.

### Decision 2: how items keep working
**Decision:** Keep every item's existing classes and data attributes (`archive-link`, `show-create-branch-modal`, `show-modal`, `data-clipboard-text`) and let `<aria-menu>` call `click()` on Enter/Space. No item handler changes.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Rewrite the item handlers to listen for `<aria-menu>` events.
- (b) Turn every item into an `<a href>` so Enter works natively.

**Rationale:** The handlers are delegated from `document` (`common-button.ts`) or bound at page load (`repo-branch.ts`, `repo-common.ts`), so they still fire when the item moves into an `<aria-menu>`. (a) would change working code for no gain. (b) can't work for items that open modals and have no URL.

**Consequences:** Easier: the diff is only template changes and tests. Harder: `repo-branch.ts` binds `.show-create-branch-modal` with `querySelectorAll` at load, so an item added later wouldn't work. That's fine today, but it should be noted in the PR's Tech Debt section.

### Scope

diff --git a/tests/e2e/repo-menus.test.ts b/tests/e2e/repo-menus.test.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..9ed8b86a8d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/e2e/repo-menus.test.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,144 @@
+import {env} from 'node:process';
+import {test, expect} from '@playwright/test';
+import type {Page} from '@playwright/test';
+import {login, apiCreateRepo, apiCreateFile, apiCreateBranch, apiEditRepo, apiHeaders, baseUrl, randomString, assertNoJsError} from './utils.ts';
+
+const owner = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER;
+
+// the archive handler POSTs to prepare the archive before downloading it
+function waitForArchivePost(page: Page, suffix: string) {
+  return page.waitForRequest((req) => req.method() === 'POST' && new URL(req.url()).pathname.endsWith(suffix));
+}
+
+test('code tab add file menu is operable by keyboard', async ({page, request}) => {
+  const repoName = `e2e-add-file-menu-${randomString(8)}`;
+  await Promise.all([apiCreateRepo(request, {name: repoName}), login(page)]);
+  await page.goto(`/${owner}/${repoName}`);
+  const trigger = page.getByRole('button', {name: 'Add File'});
+  const menu = page.getByRole('menu', {name: 'Add File'});
+
+  await trigger.focus();
+  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
+  await expect(trigger).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
+  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'New File'})).toBeFocused();
+  await page.keyboard.press('End');
+  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Apply Patch'})).toBeFocused();
+  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
+  await expect(menu).toBeHidden();
+  await expect(trigger).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
+  await expect(trigger).toBeFocused();
+
+  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
+  await page.keyboard.press('u');
+  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Upload File'})).toBeFocused();
+  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
+  await expect(page).toHaveURL(new RegExp(`/${repoName}/_upload/main/$`));
+  await assertNoJsError(page);
+});
+
+test('code tab add file menu stays shut in an archived repo', async ({page, request}) => {
+  const repoName = `e2e-add-file-archived-${randomString(8)}`;
+  await Promise.all([apiCreateRepo(request, {name: repoName}), login(page)]);
+  await apiEditRepo(request, owner, repoName, {archived: true});
+  await page.goto(`/${owner}/${repoName}`);
+  const trigger = page.getByRole('button', {name: 'Add File'});
+
+  await expect(trigger).toBeDisabled(); // a disabled button takes neither focus nor clicks
+  await trigger.focus();
+  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
+  await expect(trigger).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
+  await expect(page.getByRole('menu', {name: 'Add File'})).toBeHidden();
+});
+
+test('code tab folder menu is operable by keyboard', async ({page, request}) => {
+  const repoName = `e2e-folder-menu-${randomString(8)}`;
+  await apiCreateRepo(request, {name: repoName});
+  await Promise.all([apiCreateFile(request, owner, repoName, 'docs/readme.md', 'docs'), login(page)]);
+  await page.goto(`/${owner}/${repoName}/src/branch/main/docs`);
+  const trigger = page.getByRole('button', {name: 'More Operations'});
+
+  await trigger.focus();
+  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
+  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Copy Permalink'})).toBeFocused();
+  await page.keyboard.press('End');
+  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Delete Directory'})).toBeFocused();
+  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
+  await expect(page.getByRole('menu', {name: 'More Operations'})).toBeHidden();
+  await expect(trigger).toBeFocused();
+
+  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
+  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
+  // the browser's clipboard permission decides the text
+  await expect(page.locator('.tippy-box').filter({hasText: /Copied|Copy failed/})).toBeVisible();
+
+  await trigger.focus();
+  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
+  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
+  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Download directory as ZIP'})).toBeFocused();
+  const archivePost = waitForArchivePost(page, '/archive/main.zip');
+  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
+  await archivePost;
+  await assertNoJsError(page);
+});
+
+test('branch download menus are named and operable by keyboard', async ({page, request}) => {
+  const repoName = `e2e-branch-menu-${randomString(8)}`;
+  await apiCreateRepo(request, {name: repoName});
+  await Promise.all([apiCreateBranch(request, owner, repoName, 'feature'), login(page)]);
+  await page.goto(`/${owner}/${repoName}/branches`);
+
